# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–11 (Complete – Updated 97)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; spring of third year (auction, financial crisis, engagement rupture); military mobilization period following Napoleon's escape and landing; thaw period with frost-silvered hedges and rain threatening, early light of year; summer of third year; evening with wind off water, salt and tar smell, frost silvering hedges overnight, vespers bells, bees in lavender; early autumn with coughing sickness, dog barking, turnips on cart, river up, price of salt concerns; **late April: gusty raw day with rain whipping pavement, end of day with early light, smoke flat over fields; church service with rattling rain on windows; autumn of third year (river crossing at Quenwick); Brighton period following George-Amelia marriage (early spring/late April): turnips on cart, threatening rain, wind off water with salt and tar smell, frost-silvered hedges, flat smoke over fields, ruts and puddles after thaw; Dobbin's delayed arrival bringing news of Belgium orders; early light of year returning**
- **Primary Locations**: [All previous locations plus] **Brighton** (current setting for George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Jos Sedley's visit); Miremere and Quenwick (recent settlements by Breena Orlwood, Pebin Wexwood); Chatham (embarkation point for Belgium); Belgium (destination of ordered army deployment); Chowringhee, Calcutta (references to Jos's aspirations); Boggley Wollah (Jos's position as collector)

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher; mother French opera-girl; small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; skilled musician, linguist, artist; talented mimic
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley in City church; living with him at Brighton in "very best apartments at the inn"
- **Financial Situation**: Dunned by creditors; two abominable wretches (bailiff and man) watched greengrocer's opposite all last week; could not escape until Sunday; relies on Miss Crawley's relenting for relief
- **Talents**: Adroit treatment of duns; remarkable ability to talk creditors over; practice began almost immediately after marriage; husband finds "immense value of such a wife"
- **Current Status**: At Brighton with Rawdon; following Miss Crawley to secure her favor; emissaries continually planted at Miss Crawley's door; socializing with George and Amelia Osborne

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain in Life Guards; celebrated "blood"/dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca; at Brighton in "very best apartments at the inn"
- **Financial Status**: Bills in abundance; scarcity of ready money; deny themselves nothing; credit in plenty; good spirits despite debt; abuses dinners and wine with audacity; long custom, manly appearance, faultless boots and clothes, happy fierceness of manner serve him as well as great balance at banker's
- **Recent Activity**: Jos Sedley played billiards with him at Brighton, replenishing his purse with ready money; roars of laughter related amusing anecdotes of duns
- **Current Focus**: All hopes depend on Miss Crawley's relenting; followed her to Brighton

**Miss Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon
- **Response to Marriage**: Fainted and suffered hysterics; confined to bed under Mrs. Bute's nursing; letters unopened; not recovering from shock
- **Current Status**: At Brighton; holding out against Rawdon and Rebecca's attempts; refuses to grant them entry; emissaries from niece and nephew continually planted at her door; all of Rawdon's hopes depend on her relenting

**Mrs. Bute Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Sister-in-law to Miss Crawley; positioned as nurse; continuously present; cultivates staff loyalty; takes Miss Crawley on diversionary drives; tells stories against Rawdon and Rebecca

**Amelia Osborne (Mrs. George Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul
- **Status - MARRIED**: Married to George Osborne in chapel near Fulham Road, late April; dressed in brown silk pelisse, straw bonnet with pink ribbon, white Chantilly lace veil (gift from Jos), gold chain and watch (gift from Captain Dobbin), mother's diamond brooch
- **Honeymoon**: Enjoying "first blushing days" at Brighton with George; checked carriage as it neared three gentlemen on road, appeared nervous and blushed absurdly; expressed gladness at return; asked Jos not to be late
- **Emotional State**: Fear overcome by love at marriage; response came "fluttering up to her lips from her heart"; happy, rosy, round face; meeting constantly with Rebecca and Rawdon at Brighton; discussing marriages and life prospects with frankness and interest

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; excellent at games, billiards; over head and ears in debt; gambler, drunkster, profligate
- **Status - MARRIED**: Married Amelia Osborne in late April in chapel near Fulham Road; pale and agitated before ceremony; appeared proud and radiant after; wore blue coat and brass buttons with neat buff waistcoat
- **Honeymoon**: At Brighton with Amelia enjoying "first blushing days"; yawning at slow work, suggesting tiger-hunting to Jos; praised Jos's billiards skills; spotted Dobbin's arrival from roof and expressed delight; spoke warmly to Dobbin, shaking hand warmly; trembled for result of Dobbin's communication to father
- **Military Orders**: Received news that army is ordered to Belgium; all guards embark from Chatham next week; news came as shock to young couples
- **Father's Status**: Marriage proceeded without father's consent; Dobbin tasked with communicating marriage to John Osborne in least irritating manner possible; George anxious about father's reaction

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Role in Marriage**: Primary architect of reconciliation between George and Amelia; convinced both to proceed; urged George to act before regiment's orders; presented gold chain and watch to Amelia; groomsman to George
- **Emotional State Post-Marriage**: Felt miserable and lonely after ceremony; gave sixpences to street urchins, departed alone through rain; longed with heart-sick yearning for first few days to be over so he might see her again; left ceremony in reverie without celebration
- **Current Role**: George's plenipotentiary in London; tasked with communicating marriage to John Osborne; must call upon old Sedley and wife to keep former in good humour; must draw Jos and brother-in-law nearer to compensate for Sedley's loss of station; tasked with reconciling old Osborne to alliance
- **Brighton Visit**: Delayed arrival now effected; brought news of Belgium orders; George and Amelia delighted to see him; George asked urgent questions about Russell Square, father's reaction to marriage
- **Military Status**: Part of British army ordered to Belgium; embarkation from Chatham next week

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Status**: George married Amelia despite father's opposition; financial rupture imminent; Dobbin tasked with communicating marriage to father in least irritating manner; George trembles for result of communication; father's reaction remains unknown at this point in narrative

**John Sedley (Old Mr. Sedley)** [CHARACTER]
- Ruined merchant; declared bankrupt
- **Current Status**: Dobbin tasked with calling upon him and wife, keeping former in good humour; marriage to Osborne considered alliance that needs reconciliation with old Osborne

**Mrs. Sedley (Mary)** [CHARACTER]
- Amelia's mother; proved faithful consoler; accepted reduced circumstances; at marriage ceremony wept throughout

**Jos Sedley** [CHARACTER]
- Amelia's brother; splendid appearance; fatter than ever; "devil of a fellow at billiards"; affected military appearance and habits of late
- **At Brighton**: Made appearance in grand open carriage; played billiards with Captain Crawley, replenishing Rawdon's purse with ready money; wore military frock-coat ornamented with frogs, knobs, black buttons, meandering embroidery; walked clinking boot-spurs, swaggering prodigiously, shooting death-glances at servant girls; called Rebecca "Mrs. Crawley" in jest; fell into attitude with head lying on shoulder, grinning, one hand at back supporting on cane, other hand with diamond ring fumbling in shirt-frill; kissed diamond hand to ladies in carriage; wished all Cheltenham, Chowringhee, Calcutta could see him waving hand to beauty and in company with Rawdon Crawley

**Minor Characters**
- **Eldette Corrett**: Walked long way round to avoid muddy square; at evening chalked crooked sun on forge wall; discussed price of salt scandal with Daena
- **Breena Orlwood**: Left Quenwick and settled in Miremere
- **Pebin Wexwood**: Went along to live in Miremere as well
- **Ilzek Wexwood**: Argued with carter over price of sack of oats; only shrugged at question about rain
- **Nyrine Wexwood**: Watched clouds and predicted rain wrongly (mentioned twice)
- **Daena**: Hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step; agreed price of salt is scandal
- **Ridette Lindson**: Laughed at story nobody else found funny
- **Jotho Corrett**: Spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight
- **O'Dowd**: Goes in command of regiment to Belgium
- **Heavytop**: Has gout, mad at not being able to move with army

## Critical Facts and Status (Updated)

- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - COMPLETED AND HONEYMOON ONGOING**: Married late April in chapel near Fulham Road; enjoying "first blushing days" of honeymoon at Brighton; Amelia happy, rosy, round face; George appeared proud and radiant after ceremony
- **DOBBIN'S SACRIFICIAL ROLE - DEEPENED**: Gifts to Amelia and groomsman duties completed; left ceremony miserable and lonely; longed heart-sick for first days to be over to see her again; now assigned as George's plenipotentiary to manage marriage communication in London; tasked with keeping old Sedley in good humour, drawing Jos nearer, reconciling old Osborne to alliance
- **MARRIAGE COMMUNICATION PENDING**: Dobbin has not yet communicated marriage to John Osborne; George trembles for result; task to communicate in least irritating manner possible
- **FINANCIAL CRISIS EVIDENT**: Rawdon and Rebecca dunned by creditors; bailiffs watched greengrocer's opposite all last week; Rebecca's talent for talking over creditors now essential; rely on Miss Crawley's relenting; despite debt, maintain "very best apartments at the inn" at Brighton; Jos's billiards losses replenished Rawdon's purse temporarily
- **MILITARY ORDERS RECEIVED**: British army ordered to Belgium to pursue Napoleon; all guards embark from Chatham next week; news came as shock to George and Amelia and "all these gentlemen"; Heavytop has gout and mad at inability to move; O'Dowd goes in command; regiment mobilization imminent
- **MISS CRAWLEY STILL HOLDING OUT**: Followed to Brighton by Rawdon and Rebecca; refuses entry; emissaries continually planted at her door; all Rawdon's hopes depend on her relenting; Mrs. Bute continues nursing and company
- **SOCIAL CONNECTIONS FORMING**: George and Amelia meeting constantly with Rawdon and Rebecca at Brighton; discussing marriages and life prospects frankly; gentlemen playing piquet while wives chat; Jos Sedley's billiards play with Rawdon providing temporary financial relief
